items.text: Police arrested a 45-year-old man on the suspicion of trying to steal an original copy of the Magna Carta from Salisbury Cathedral in southern England. The cathedral houses one of only four remaining copies of the Magna Carta, which is one of the most important legal manuscripts in the world. King John of England signed it in 1215 AD, and it enshrined the basic rights on the principle that no one is above the law – not even England’s kings and queens. Alarms activated when a man smashed the glass box with the document inside. Luckily, it was undamaged during the incident, but people have temporarily removed it. Difficult words: suspicion (a belief – the police are not sure it was him), legal (relating to the law), manuscripts (a handwritten document), enshrine (preserve in a form that will be protected and respected), temporarily (for some time, not forever). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Magna Carta is one of the most important legal manuscripts in the world. King John of England signed it in 1215 AD. It enshrined the power of law – the fact that no one is above the law, not even kings or queens. There are only four copies of the Magna Carta left, and one of them is in Salisbury Cathedral in southern England. Alarms activated when a man broke the glass box with the document. Police arrested the 45-year-old man who probably tried to steal this manuscript. Luckily, the document was undamaged. Difficult words: legal (relating to the law), manuscript (a handwritten document), enshrine (preserve in a form that will be protected and respected). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Magna Carta is a very important document. It is a legal document. It says that no one is above the law. This is even for kings or queens. People create it in 1215 AD in England. Today, there are only four copies of the Magna Carta. One copy is in Salisbury Cathedral in southern England. It is inside a glass box. The alarms activate when the glass is broken. A man tries to steal the document. However, police stop him. They arrest him. He is 45 years old. Difficult words: legal (about the law), create (make), activate (turn on), steal (take). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Yemen, there has been a civil war for three years, something which the UN described as the ‘world’s worst humanitarian crisis’. More than 10,000 people died in this war. The war is between pro-government, Saudi Arabia- backed coalition and the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels. The Houthis captured the city of Hodeida, which is the chief port of Yemen in 2015. The Saudi-led coalition is trying to take this city back and launched airstrikes on the city. Fighting in the port prevents food and aid from reaching the country’s civilians , and airstrikes hit schools, hospitals, and even wedding parties. Many Yemeni civilians died. The Houthis responded by firing long-range missiles at Saudi Arabia. Difficult words: back (support, help), coalition (a group of people working on a goal), launch (start), prevent from (stop something from happening), civilian (a person who is not in the military). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The civil war in Yemen started three years ago, and more than 10,000 people died from it. The war is between a pro-government coalition and the Houthi rebels. Saudi Arabia backs the coalition, and Iran backs the Houthis. In 2015, the Houthis captured Hodeida, which is an important port in Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition is trying to take this port city back, and recently it launched airstrikes . Since Hodeida is a port, things and food cannot get to people. Many people also die in the airstrikes, and schools, hospitals, and even wedding parties are hit. In response, the Houthis fire missiles at Saudi Arabia. Difficult words: civil war (a war between the people of one country), coalition (a group of people that agree to work on something), launch (start), airstrike (an attack from a plane). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a civil war in Yemen. It starts in 2015. Saudi Arabia backs one side . Iran backs the other side. Right now, there is a fight for Hodeida. Hodeida is an important port city. Due to the fighting, people cannot get food. Many people die in the city. Schools and hospitals are hit by the war. This war is terrible. Between 2015 and 2018, 10,000 people die. Difficult words: civil war (a war between the people of one country), back (help), side (a group of people), port (a place by the sea where ships can come and bring things or people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People found a never-before-seen shipwreck off the coast of Bulgaria in the Black Sea. Scientists believe that one of the wrecks is a 2,400-year-old Greek trading vessel . Edward Price from the Black Sea Maritime Archaeology Project said that there are ships at the bottom of the ocean that people have never seen; we have only seen them in paintings, murals and books. The oxygen-free environment means that the wrecks are extremely well preserved, and the recent findings led to their own documentary project at the British Museum. Difficult words: vessel (a ship or large a boat), mural (a painting on the surface of a wall). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists found ancient shipwrecks at the bottom of the Black Sea off of Bulgaria, and they believe that one of the wrecks is 2,400 years old and was a Greek trading vessel . The shipwrecks were in such deep water that there is no oxygen, and this means they are very well-preserved . This is the first time people can have a look at ships this old. Before, we could only see them in books or in paintings. Difficult words: ancient (very old), vessel (a ship or large boat), well-preserved (not destroyed). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists find shipwrecks . They are at the bottom of the Black Sea. The ships are around 2,400 years old. One of them is a trading ship . The ships are in very deep water. There is no oxygen there. Due to this, the ships still look good. Difficult words: shipwreck (a ship which is broken), trading ship (a ship for moving things and making business). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A vintage single-engine plane crash landed on a motorway in California, and it burst into flames after the emergency landing. Fire crews managed to safely remove the pilot before the flames engulfed the plane. The cause of the dramatic crash is not unknown. Difficult words: vintage (old and high in quality), engulf (cover completely). You can watch the video news lower on this page.30

In California, a plane crash landed on a motorway. It was a vintage single-engine plane that burst into flames right after landing. Luckily, fire crews removed the pilot in time. The cause of the incident is unknown. Difficult words: vintage (old and high in quality), burst into flames (get on fire), cause (why something happened). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A plane lands on a motorway. This is not normal. It is a crash landing. The motorway is in California. The plane has one engine . It is a vintage plane. The plane is on fire after it lands. Luckily, people save the pilot. We do not know the cause of this incident . Difficult words: engine (the part of a plane or a car which makes it move), vintage (old and high in quality), cause (the reason), incident (when something happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The construction of the world’s longest cross-sea bridge finished and it opened last Tuesday. The Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge is 55 kilometres long, and it reduces travel time from 4 hours to just 45 minutes. People originally scheduled the launch for 2016, but the bridge was beset by a variety of problems. Many Hong Kong activists see the project as a political statement. Hong Kong politician Claudia Mo said that Hong Kong is already connected to mainland China in every way (land, air and sea). Yet China, she claimed , needed the bridge as a political symbol to remind Hongkongers that they are connected to the motherland . Difficult words: launch (opening), beset (troubled), claim (state, argue), motherland (the country of origin). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Tuesday, people finished the longest cross-sea bridge and it opened. The Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge is 55 kilometres long, and it reduces travel time from 4 hours to just 45 minutes. Many Hong Kong activists see the project as a political statement . One Hong Kong politician said that Hong Kong is already connected to China in every way. She claimed that China needed the bridge as a political symbol to remind Hongkongers that they are connected to the motherland . Difficult words: statement (a symbol), claim (say, argue), remind (show), motherland (the original country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China builds a cross-sea bridge. It is the longest in the world. Now China finishes it. The bridge is open. It is 55 kilometres long. It connects Hong Kong, Zhuhai and Macao. It cuts travel time from 4 hours to 45 minutes. Many Hong Kong activists see the bridge symbolically . It shows Hongkongers that they are connected to China. Difficult words: activist (a person who does things for politics), symbolically (like a symbol – something which is not important for what it does, but it is important for what it says about something), connected (together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A train carrying around 366 passengers from Taipei to Taitung derailed last Sunday, killing at least 22 people and injuring 171 others. The Puyuma express is a type of railway service on Taiwan Railways launched in 2013, and it travels up to 150 kilometres per hour. One hundred and twenty soldiers are working alongside firefighters with cranes to help find trapped people, and others are investigating the cause of the derailment. Difficult words: launch (open), derail (leave the tracks). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A train going from Taipei to Taitung in Taiwan derailed last Sunday. It was carrying around 366 passengers, and the derailment killed at least 22 people and injured 171 others. The express launched in 2013, and the trains travel up to 150 kilometre per hour. Soldiers and firefighters are working to find trapped people. People are investigating the cause of this crash. Difficult words: derail (leave the tracks), express (a very fast service), launch (open), trapped (under something heavy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Taipei and Taitung are cities in Taiwan. A train goes from Taipei to Taitung. It carries 366 passengers. This train derails . Twenty-two or more people die. One hundred and seventy-one people are injured . Some people are trapped . Soldiers and firefighters try to save them. Difficult words: derail (when a train car leaves the tracks), injured (have problems with the body), trapped (under something heavy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel has a food craze that is a cross-cultural concoction : a restaurant in the city of Rishon Lezion changed the regular chickpeas and pita to a Belgian waffle. A cook at the restaurant said that the food is similar because the waffle is made from falafel but different because no oil or frying is involved. Half of a waffle with fillings like tahini and vegetables costs about £6.30 or $8.17. There was a long line on the fifth day of the restaurant being open. Difficult words: craze (something very popular), concoction (mixture), chickpea (a round yellowish edible seed), tahini (a sesame paste that people use in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean food). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Israel, a popular food trend from two cultures started when a restaurant changed the regularly used chickpeas and pita to a Belgian waffle. A cook at the restaurant said that the food is similar because the waffle is made from falafel . However, the restaurant does not use oil or fry the falafel. Half of a waffle with fillings like tahini and vegetables costs about £6.30 or $8.17. A long line was at the restaurant on the fifth day of the restaurant being open. Difficult words: chickpea (a yellowish type of pea that people use in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean food), pita (a type of bread that you can split open to put food inside), falafel (a food made from chickpeas and usually eaten in pita), tahini (a thick sauce made from sesame seeds). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Israel, a restaurant is trying a new food idea. It is very popular. It has ideas from Israeli and Belgian foods. The restaurant changes the food that it normally uses. It normally uses chickpeas and pita to make food that is like a sandwich. Now, it uses a Belgian waffle . The waffle is made out of falafel . Half of a waffle with food inside costs about £6.30 or $8.17. People like the food. There is a long line in front of the restaurant. Difficult words: chickpea (a pea that people use in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean food), pita (a bread that you can open to put food inside), Belgian waffle (a large waffle made in a machine that has small squares), falafel (a food made from chickpeas and usually eaten in pita). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Baqaa, Jordan, a refugee camp’s walls show stories in graffiti by artist Khali Gheith about the camp where he was born. He also narrates the lives of the people living there through his artwork. He says that as a Palestinian artist, he ‘must document the Palestinian struggle’ and show the ‘great crime against the Palestinian people’. He does his art in the streets so that children can see it and ‘remember their national value ’. In addition to walls, Gheith’s work is on display at the Yarmouk Baqqa Club, which is the heart of the camp. Difficult words: narrate (tell a story), struggle (a continuous fight, a conflict), national value (the important beliefs of a people and their country). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In a city in Jordan, graffiti is on the walls of a refugee camp, and the artist narrates the story of the camp and of the lives of the people living there in his artwork. He says that as a Palestinian artist, he ‘documents the Palestinian struggle ’ and shows the ‘great crime against the Palestinian people’. He does his art in the streets so that children can remember the important beliefs from their country. In addition to walls, the artist’s work is on display at a club, which is the heart of the camp. Difficult words: narrate (tell a story), struggle (a continuous fight, a long conflict). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Palestinians live in a city in Jordan. They live in a refugee camp . One Palestinian is an artist. He creates graffiti on the walls. He tells a story about the refugee camp. He tells stories about the people who live there. He says that he is a Palestinian artist. This means that he has to tell the stories about the Palestinian struggle . He says that he makes his art in the streets so that children can see it. They can remember the important ideas from their country. People can see his art at a club, too. The club is an important area of the camp. Difficult words: refugee camp (a place where refugees live), refugee (a person who has to leave his or her country because of danger), struggl e (a long fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kakao, the operator of South Korea’s top chat app, is launching an Uber-like carpooling service in the country. The app will connect drivers with passengers during commuting hours. Korean taxi drivers fear that the service could put thousands of their jobs at risk, and tens of thousands of them held a massive rally in central Seoul. One protester said that the app grants the permission to do business with personal vehicles without taxi registration – the driver’s stance was that the government could not impose the same law on unregistered drivers and taxi drivers alike . Difficult words: launch (start), carpool (share a ride with somebody), commut e (travel to work or school or somewhere), impose (put in place), alike (in the same way). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An Uber-like app is launching in South Korea that will connect drivers with passengers so that they can share a ride. Korean taxi drivers fear that the service could put thousands of their jobs at risk. Tens of thousands of them held a massive rally in central Seoul. Difficult words: launch (start), rally (a protest). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Uber is an app . It lets you call a car. You can also be an Uber driver. You can drive people to make money. An app like Uber is launching in South Korea. Taxi drivers fear for their jobs. They protest in central Seoul. Tens of thousands of them come. Difficult words: app (a program in your smartphone), launch (start). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An official report on an incident at the San Francisco Airport in 2017 has been released , as it reveals a near-miss which could have been the worst accident in aviation history. The video shows an Air Canada plane approaching to land on a taxiway where four planes were already sitting. After realising the mistake, the pilot managed to avoid the other planes by only a few feet. Passengers on five airplanes could have died or been seriously injured. Luckily, nobody was harmed . Difficult words: reveal (show), aviation (relating to airplanes), approach (get closer), taxiway (a road for planes to move around an airport), avoid (get away from), harm (injure). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2017, an incident happened at the San Francisco Airport, and people released a report about it just recently. An airplane was approaching the airport to land when the pilot mistook the runway for a taxiway with four airplanes already sitting there! Luckily, the pilot managed to avoid the other planes but with only a few feet between them! Difficult words: release (show people), approach (get closer), taxiway (a road for planes to move around an airport), avoid (get away from). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A plane wants to land in San Francisco. It gets closer and closer to the airport. However, it is not getting closer to the runway . It is getting closer to a taxiway . This is a terrible mistake. There are four planes on the taxiway. The lives of many people are in danger. Luckily, the plane avoids the other planes. Nobody is hurt. Difficult words: runway (a road at an airport where planes land and take off), taxiway (a road for planes to move around an airport), avoid (move away from, not hit). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The queen’s grandchild, Princess Eugenie, got married recently, and two of the guests were Prince Harry and his wife Meghan who wore a dress that gave rise to rumours of her being pregnant. This is because she usually wears a more closely- tailored style. The couple confirmed the rumours shortly after Harry and Meghan touched down in Sydney, Australia. The couple are down under for 16 day, visiting Australia, Fiji, Tonga and New Zealand. Difficult words: rumour (when people say something that can be true or not), tailored (fitted), touch down (land in an aeroplane), down under informal (Australia and New Zealand). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Meghan, Prince Harry’s wife, usually wears closely-fitted dresses, and when this changed, people started a rumour that she is pregnant . Harry and Meghan confirmed this rumour recently in Sydney, as they are there on a 16-day trip. They are visiting Australia, Fiji, Tonga and New Zealand. Difficult words: rumour (when people say something that can be true or not), pregnant (with a baby inside), confirm (say that something is true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Meghan is Prince Harry’s wife. People start a rumour . They say that she is pregnant . Harry and Meghan travel to Sydney. They say that the rumour is true. Meghan is pregnant. Harry and Meghan are in Australia for 16 days. They also visit Fiji, Tonga and New Zealand. Difficult words: rumour (something which people say that can be true or not true), pregnant (with a baby inside). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Aerial and underwater footage shows Sea World rescuers free a whale calf which became caught in shark nets off of Australia’s Gold Coast. The calf’s mother swam around its baby as rescuers arrived at the scene and got to work. The disentanglement was successful and the animal was free after 45 minutes. The calf only had some superficial wounds from its ordeal , and people later saw it s wimming away with its mother after they released it. Difficult words: aerial (from the air), calf (a young whale or a cow), disentanglement (the act of disentangling – freeing something that they are entangled with – caught in), superficial (on the top surface, not deep), ordeal (a difficult event). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A whale calf was caught in shark nets off Australia’s Gold Coast, and rescuers arrived at the scene to get to work. It took them 45 minutes to free the whale. The mother swam around as they worked. The little whale had only superficial wounds , and later people saw it swimming away with its mother. Difficult words: calf (a young whale), scene (the place where there something happens, such as a problem), superficial wounds (cut which are not deep). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a whale calf . It gets caught in shark nets. It happens off of Australia’s Gold Coast. People help the calf. They arrive at the scene . They start to work. They work for 45 minutes. The whale mother is nearby. She swims around. After 45 minutes, the calf is free. It swims away with its mother. Difficult words: calf (a young whale), arrive (come to a place), scene (the place where something happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Several months’ worth of rain fell in one night in southwestern France which led to flash floods , and streams became a raging torrents that washed away roads. Schools were closed and local authorities are urging people to stay at home. Thirteen lives have been lost in the floods – four deaths were clustered around the town of Villegailhenc. Difficult words: flash flood (a sudden local flood), stream (a small river), raging (very powerful), torrent (a lot of fast-moving water), urge (ask strongly), clustered (positioned). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Several months’ worth of rain fell in one night in southwestern France which led to flash floods . Small rivers became raging torrents that washed away roads. Schools were closed and people had to stay at home. Thirteen people died, and four of them died near the town of Villegailhenc. Difficult words: flash flood (a sudden local flood), raging torrent (very powerful, fast-moving water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It rains a lot in southern France. The amount of water is extreme. Water, which normally rains in months, falls down in a night. This leads to flash floods . Small rivers become raging torrents . Roads are washed away. Thirteen people die. Difficult words: amount (how much of something), flash flood (a lot of water which comes quickly because of a lot of rain), raging torrent (a lot of powerful water which moves very fast). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A dog came onto the football pitch for three minutes in Gori, Georgia, during a National Football League game between Torpedo Kutaisi and Dila Gori. The dog stopped the game and delighted fans, as it wanted to play with the athletes. Eventually, David Khurtsilava directed it off the field by acting playful with it. The teams scored 0-0 in this game. Difficult words: delight (entertain, make very happy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Georgia, a dog came onto a football pitch for three minutes during a game. It stopped the game and delighted fans, as it wanted to play with the athletes . Eventually, one player directed it off the field by acting playful with it. The teams scored 0-0 in this game. Difficult words: delight (make very happy), athlete (someone playing a sport), direct (tell someone what to do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Georgia, a football game is happening. A dog comes onto the football pitch . It stops the game. It wants to play with the football players. It delights the fans. It runs around for three minutes. One player runs with it off the field. The teams score 0-0 in this game. Difficult words: pitch (the area where people playa sport), delight (make happy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An adorable baby silvery gibbon was born at Chester Zoo in Cheshire, England, to mom Tiu and dad Alven. This is good news as there are less than 2,500 of the endangered animals in the wild. Zoo keepers do not yet know if the baby is male or female because it is too tiny to tell. This baby is the newest one in a baby boom at the zoo. Difficult words: adorable (extremely cute), endangered (in danger of dying out), tiny (very small). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An adorable baby silvery gibbon was born at Chester Zoo in Cheshire, England. There are less than 2,500 of the endangered animals in the wild, so this is good news. Zoo keepers do not know if the baby is male or female because it is too small to tell. This baby is the newest baby in a baby boom at the zoo. Difficult words: adorable (very cute), endangered (in danger of dying out), baby boom (when many babies are born at one time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This happens in England. A cute baby silvery gibbon is born at a zoo. This is good news. There are less than 2,500 of the endangered animals in nature. Zoo keepers do not know if this baby is male or female. The baby is too small to know. Many babies are born at this zoo right now. This baby is the newest one. The zoo is having a baby boom . Difficult words: silvery gibbon (a type of small grey ape – an animal that is related to people), endangered (when a type of plant or animal is in danger of dying out), baby boom (when many babies are born at the same time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Military and emergency services are continuing to search for missing people caught in the flash floods on the Spanish island of Mallorca. At least ten people died in the disaster caused by torrential rain . Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez flew in to support the emergency services, and tennis player Rafael Nadal joined the recovery efforts. People filmed Nadal helping residents clear mud from their houses left by the rainstorms. He also opened up his tennis academy on the island for those in need of shelter . Difficult words: torrential rain (extremely heavy rain over a short period of time), shelter (a place to stay). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Torrential rain caused flash floods on the Spanish island of Mallorca, and at least ten people died and more are missing. Spain’s prime minister flew to Mallorca and tennis player Rafael Nadal joined the recovery efforts . People filmed him clearing mud from a house, and he also opened up his tennis academy for those who need a place to stay. Difficult words: torrential rain (extremely heavy rain), flash flood (a lot of water which comes quickly usually from rain), recovery efforts (doing things to help make things normal again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Torrential rain causes flash floods on Mallorca. Mallorca is a Spanish island. Ten people die. More people are missing. People are trying to make things normal again. Spain’s prime minister flies to Mallorca to show his help. Tennis player Rafael Nadal helps, too. He helps with the cleaning. He also helps people who have no homes. They can stay at his tennis academy. Difficult words: torrential rain (very heavy rain), cause (make something happen), flash flood (a lot of water which comes quickly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A huge lunar meteorite that crashed down to Earth thousands of years ago is going up for auction and people expect it to sell for over half a million dollars. Tricia Eaton, the auctioneer , said that it felt incredible to hold a piece of the moon. The rock is special because of its size – lunar meteorites found on Earth are usually as big as an apple. People found the 5.4-kilogram rock in a desert in Mauritania (a country in north western Africa) last year. Difficult words: huge (very big), lunar (of or from the moon), auctioneer (a person who manages auctions), incredible (amazing). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A huge lunar meteorite crashed down to Earth thousands of years ago, and people discovered it in a desert in Mauritania last year. Mauritania is a country in Northwestern Africa. Now the 5.4-kilogram rock is going on auction, and people think that it will sell for more than 500,000 dollars because it is so big. Lunar meteorites are usually about as big as an apple, and it is something special to hold a piece of the moon in your hands too. Difficult words: huge (very big), lunar (from the moon), discover (find). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A lunar meteorite falls down to Earth. This is thousands of years ago . Last year, people find this meteorite. They find it in Mauritania. This is a country in north western Africa. The meteorite is 5.4 kilograms heavy. It is much bigger than other lunar meteorites. Most lunar meteorites are only as big as an apple. The big meteorite goes on auction. It can sell for 500,000 dollars or more. Difficult words: lunar (from the moon), meteorite (a rock which falls down from space), ago (before). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hurricane Michael is the strongest hurricane to make landfall in the continental US since 1992, and it has killed at least 17 people. Michael wreaked havoc across the south-eastern states of America, completely reducing one town in Florida to rubble . It left only a few buildings standing after the 250 kilometre-per-hour winds hit the coastal town of 1,072 residents. Difficult words: make landfall (arrive at land), continental (in a continent), wreak havoc (destroy everything), rubble (in broken pieces). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hurricane Michael is the strongest hurricane to hit the USA since 1992, and it has killed at least 17 people. Michael wreaked havoc across the south-eastern states of America. It completely destroyed one town in Florida, and left only a few buildings standing. The winds reached speeds of up to 250 kilometres per hour. Difficult words: wreak havoc (destroy everything). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hurricane Michael hits the USA. It is the strongest hurricane since 1992. The winds blow 250 kilometres per hour. The hurricane kills 17 people. It completely destroys one town in Florida. Only a few buildings are OK. Difficult words: since (from), blow (move by wind), destroy (break). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Canberra region in Australia has been experiencing an increase in the number of orphaned joeys and malnourished animals due to prolonged droughts . Philip Machin, President of Wildcare, which is a volunteer organisation dedicated to rescue, rehabilitation and release of Australian native wildlife, said that it had 378 kangaroos come into care in the last financial year. Two years ago, it only had 270 kangaroos. The orphans require a special blend of milk to keep them alive in the first 18 months of life, and rehabilitating and raising a single joey costs 500 Australian Dollars (around 350 USD). The wildlife charity needs to raise around $40,000 to be able to cope with the increased demand. Difficult words: joey (a young kangaroo), malnourished (suffering from not having enough food), due to (because of), drought (a time when the weather is very dry). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the Canberra region in Australia, there are more orphaned joeys because of long, dry weather. One organisation said that it had 378 kangaroos come into care in the last financial year. Two years ago, it only had 270 kangaroos. The orphans need special milk to keep them alive in the first 18 months of life. Rehabilitating and raising one single joey costs 500 Australian Dollars (around 350 USD). The charity needs to raise around $40,000 to be able to deal with more of the joeys. Difficult words: orphaned (alone, without parents or another animal or person to help or to take care), joey (a young kangaroo), deal with (be able to care for something, work on a problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It is dry in Australia. Due to the dry weather, there are more orphaned joeys . One organisation is helping 378 joeys now. Two years ago, it was only 270. It is not cheap to take care of a joey. The organisation needs help. It needs more money. It needs around $40,000. Difficult words: orphaned (alone, without parents or another animal or person to help), joey (a young kangaroo), was (the past of ‘is’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Relatives paid tribute to their loved ones after 20 people died when a limousine lost control and crashed in the USA. Authorities said that it was the worst US road traffic accident in nearly a decade. An aunt of one of the victims said that she hoped that they did not suffer and that their death was instant. The limousine was carrying a group of four sisters and their friends to a 30th birthday celebration. Difficult words: pay tribute (show respect). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
